_comment: R3-06 claims-audit wave, probes for batches 1-3 (27 skills, 75 contradicted claims). One probe per contradicted-claim class the writer+reviewer recipe fixed. Arm A = model alone, arm B = model + the owning skill's SKILL.md + llm-anti-patterns.md (run_lift). Quotes are verbatim lines from scratchpad/corpus264 (264) or scratchpad/corpus (262, Apex Reference / Security Guide). Built 2026-10-20.

probes.question: Does Schema.DescribeFieldResult.getPicklistValues() return inactive picklist values as well as active ones?
probes.wrong_answer: Yes, it returns every value including inactive ones; filter with isActive().
probes.correct_answer: No. It returns only active PicklistEntry objects; inactive values are not in the list.
probes.quote: Returns a list of active PicklistEntry objects.
probes.wrong_source: skill before audit: 'getPicklistValues() returns inactive values' + a checker isActive rule

probes.question: When Apex reads a protected custom metadata type record with getInstance() or getAll(), is a long text field returned in full?
probes.wrong_answer: Yes, getInstance() returns the complete field values of the record.
probes.correct_answer: No. Only the first 255 characters of any field are returned; use a SOQL query to read the full value.
probes.quote: Only the first 255 characters are returned for any field in a custom metadata type record, so longer text
probes.wrong_source: skill before audit: read secrets with getInstance() with no truncation note

probes.question: In CustomObject metadata for a custom metadata type, which element and value make the type readable only by Apex inside the managed package?
probes.correct_answer: <visibility>PackageProtected</visibility> (custom metadata types only, API 47.0 and later); Protected hides it from subscriber orgs but not from the package's own org admins.
probes.quote: PackageProtected— (Custom metadata type only) It’s only accessible by the custom Apex code in the package.

probes.question: How do you expose an Apex method to JavaScript remoting in Visualforce: with a Visualforce component or an Apex annotation?
probes.wrong_answer: Add an <apex:remoteAction> component to the page and point it at the controller method.
probes.correct_answer: With the @RemoteAction annotation on a static Apex method; there is no <apex:remoteAction> component.
probes.quote: The RemoteAction annotation provides support for Apex methods used in Visualforce to be called via JavaScript.
probes.wrong_source: skill before audit: <apex:remoteAction> in SKILL.md, well-architected and the template

probes.question: Do Visualforce custom controllers enforce the running user's object and field-level permissions, or must the developer add those checks manually?
probes.wrong_answer: Custom controllers run in system mode, so the developer must manually enforce CRUD, FLS and sharing.
probes.correct_answer: Standard and custom controllers execute entirely in user mode, so object and field-level permissions of the current user are enforced (system mode by default applied only at API 66.0 and earlier).
probes.quote: both standard and custom controllers execute entirely in user mode, in which the object and field-level
probes.wrong_source: skill before audit: 'custom controllers must manually enforce sharing/FLS/CRUD'

probes.question: From which API version is Database.queryWithBinds available?
probes.correct_answer: API 57.0 and later (55.0 introduced only the accessLevel parameter on Database.query).
probes.quote: (API version 57.0 and later) Another option is to use the Database.queryWithBinds method.

probes.question: How many levels of parent-to-child relationship can a single SOQL query traverse in API 58.0 and later?
probes.wrong_answer: One: a subquery cannot itself contain a subquery.
probes.correct_answer: Up to five levels of parent-to-child relationship (two levels at API 57.0 and earlier).
probes.quote: In API version 58.0 and later, up to five levels of parent-to-child relationship can be queried via REST,
probes.wrong_source: skill before audit: 'a subquery cannot itself contain a subquery'

probes.question: Can a custom Apex sharing reason be defined on a standard object such as Account, and from which API version?
probes.wrong_answer: No. Sharing reasons exist only for custom objects; standard objects can only use the Manual row cause.
probes.correct_answer: Yes, from API 68.0 (Winter '27). Before that, sharing reasons were available only for custom objects (API 14.0+), and standard objects had to use Manual.
probes.quote: Sharing reasons for standard objects are available in API version 68.0 and later.
probes.wrong_source: skill before audit: 'standard objects have no reasons'

probes.question: At API 67.0 and later, how does an Apex class with no sharing keyword (neither with sharing nor without sharing) run?
probes.correct_answer: It runs in with sharing mode; the older caller-determined behaviour applies only at API 66.0 and earlier.
probes.quote: In API version 67.0 and later, classes without an explicit sharing declaration run in with sharing mode.
probes.wrong_source: skill before audit: 'a class with no sharing keyword defaults to without sharing'

probes.question: Which custom field data types can be marked External ID in Salesforce?
probes.wrong_answer: Any field type, including Long Text Area.
probes.correct_answer: Only auto number, email, number and text fields.

probes.wrong_source: skill example before audit: 'Value__c (Long Text Area, External ID)'
